findings.documented: project_id links the listing to a builder project, and is null for resale property that is not part of one
findings.actual: listings sharing the same project_id are frequently in completely different buildings and locations. Example: project_id P40276 links listings from 4 different named buildings (Prestige Vista, SHRIRAM CREST, Rohan Park, Aparna Heights), 13-25 km apart despite all being tagged locality=velachery. The most extreme case found had linked listings 8,172 km apart. The project record for P40276 itself is named 'Brigade Meadows', which matches none of its 12 linked listings' apartment names.
findings.how_found: measured pairwise distances between listings sharing the same project_id, expecting them to be physically close since they claim to belong to the same builder project; found distances inconsistent with any real geographic grouping
findings.impact: project_id cannot be trusted to identify listings belonging to the same real building or project. This affects any analysis relying on project_id for grouping, including the reported total_listings count per project and identifying a project's actual price range

findings.documented: Returns active sale listings in your city. Inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side, so anything this endpoint returns is safe to show to a user.
findings.actual: 867 of 4,100 retrievable listing records (21%) have is_live: false, meaning inactive listings are NOT excluded by the server as claimed. The is_live field itself is also undocumented — it does not appear anywhere in the documented listing object.
findings.how_found: counted is_live values across the full deduplicated dataset after confirming pagination correctness
findings.impact: a frontend trusting the documentation's claim would show inactive/withdrawn listings to users as if they were live and available, contradicting the stated 'safe to show to a user' guarantee

findings.documented: N/A — no explicit claim, but implies listing data should be internally consistent and usable
findings.actual: 45 listing records describe physically impossible properties across 5 distinct, disjoint error types (9 records each): floor exceeding total_floors, carpet_area exceeding super_built_up_area, negative price, swapped latitude/longitude coordinates (raw values around lat=80/lon=13, which correct perfectly into valid Chennai bounds when swapped), and posted_at dates in the future. Errors are spread across all 5 source websites and multiple property types, with no single pattern dominating. Separately, 138 records with floor=0/total_floors=0 and 147 records with bedroom=0 were investigated and confirmed to be legitimate plot listings (property_type=plot), not corrupt data — 3 of the 45 corrupt records happen to also be plots with an unrelated separate error.
findings.how_found: ran isolated impossibility checks per field combination on the full deduplicated dataset; manually verified borderline cases (floor=0, bedroom=0) against property_type before excluding them from the corrupt set
findings.impact: these 45 records cannot represent real properties and would mislead users or break any pricing/area-based calculations if not filtered out

findings.documented: N/A — no explicit claim about listing authenticity
findings.actual: 93 listing records show a combined pattern consistent with enquiry-generating fake listings: their posted_by_contact number appears on 15+ unrelated listings spanning different apartment names, localities, and property types (inconsistent with a single legitimate agent's coherent portfolio, unlike contacts with 10-12 listings which showed varied but coherent real portfolios), AND their price is 40-70% below the median price-per-sqft for their locality+bedroom group (a 'too good to be true' price, but not extreme enough to be an obvious data-entry error).
findings.how_found: cross-referenced contact-number reuse frequency against price-per-sqft deviation from locality+bedroom medians; validated the reuse-count cutoff of 15 by manually inspecting boundary cases (10-12 listings per contact showed coherent varied portfolios; 15+ showed scattered unrelated properties)
findings.impact: these listings would generate enquiries to numbers that likely do not represent genuine, available properties, wasting user trust and time

findings.documented: Money: Indian rupees, integer, everywhere in the API
findings.actual: 8 listing records had price entered in thousands of rupees rather than full rupees (e.g. price=9430 for a property whose correct value is ₹94,30,000). Confirmed by multiplying by 1000: all 8 corrected prices fall in ₹72.4L–1.63Cr and produce price-per-sqft values (₹7,574–11,572) clustered tightly around the dataset median of ₹9,681/sqft. These records are corrected (price ×1000) and treated as valid listings, not excluded.
findings.how_found: computed price-per-sqft by locality+bedroom group and found a small cluster at roughly 0.1% of the group median; tested ×100 and ×1000 multipliers, confirmed ×1000 restores all 8 to realistic market-rate values
findings.impact: without correction these listings display prices ~1000x too low, making them appear impossibly cheap and skewing any price-based calculations or user-facing displays

findings.documented: Area: Square feet, integer, everywhere in the API
findings.actual: 326 listing records (predominantly sourced from magichomes) have both carpet_area and super_built_up_area reported in square metres instead of the documented square feet. Confirmed because their internal carpet/SBA ratio (~75%) exactly matches the normal ratio seen across all other portals, and converting both fields by 10.764 (sqm-to-sqft) produces realistic values (300-3,000 sqft, ₹3,000-20,000/sqft) consistent with the rest of the dataset.
findings.how_found: flagged as physically-impossible-tiny during Q6 outlier analysis; disproved via ratio comparison that it was a garbage/impossible value, then confirmed unit mismatch by successful correction
findings.impact: listings would display area values roughly 90% smaller than reality if not corrected, making legitimate properties look impossibly cramped and skewing any area or price-per-sqft based calculations
